summary.headline: Oswal Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue fell 7.9% YoY to INR474 crore and operating EBITDA margin dropped to 15.7%, while FY27 guidance of 20-25% growth was maintained.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR474 crore, down 7.9% YoY and 7.1% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR82 crore (17.1% margin) and operating EBITDA of INR74 crore (15.7%). Management attributed the margin fall to a 9% price reduction in Magel Tyala tenders, higher raw material costs from geopolitical factors, and module sales through the channel, partly offset by value engineering. Receivable days rose to 229 from 155, pushing the cash conversion cycle to 244 days from 172. Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% and an operating EBITDA margin of 15-17%, while relying on PM KUSUM 2.0 timing and the PM Surya Ghar rooftop business for the second half.

financial_highlights.value: INR266 crore; net debt/equity 0.15x; net debt/operating EBITDA 0.90x

vs ~40,400 in Q4 FY26 and ~56,000 in Q1 FY26

segments.name: PM KUSUM / Magel Tyala solar pumps
segments.commentary: Core business; order book of 22,025 pumps, with near-term pipeline of ~12,500 pumps across direct PM KUSUM, Magel Tyala, indirect PM KUSUM and exports. Magel Tyala price cuts of ~9% were the biggest margin drag.

segments.name: Solar EPC / PM Surya Ghar (rooftop, utility, C&I)
segments.commentary: Order book ~72 MW with 359 MW pipeline. Dedicated PM Surya Ghar vertical formed; internal target of ~2 lakh installations in FY27, implying INR800-1,000 crore revenue per management. Negligible contribution in Q1; expected to start from Q2.

segments.name: Wires and cables / channel sales
segments.commentary: Management expects INR70-100 crore revenue from wires and cables this year, using existing in-house spare capacity with no significant capex; margins expected to be below KUSUM pumps.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% over FY26 maintained, back-ended; Q2 YoY growth expected at 10-15%.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 15-17%; PAT margin guided at 11-13%. Guidance assumes current bids and excludes any PM KUSUM 2.0 upside, which management says would lift margins slightly.
Medium-term growth target of 30-40% after FY27.
Receivables expected to be better in Q2 than Q1 and significantly better in Q3; cash conversion cycle not expected to change sharply in Q2.
PM KUSUM 2.0 launch expected in Q2 FY27 per management, but IR advisor said no one can guarantee August timing.
Inverter in-house production expected within ~6 months; field trials for prototype in ~2 months.
capex_capacity: 1 GW of solar module capacity already invested; commercial production expected by first or second week of September 2026 (first phase of expansion).
Remaining module expansion (total 1.5 GW referenced in question) progressing; management says a 1-2 month gap possible due to rain.
Pump and motor capacity expansion and automation to complete by Q3 FY27.
Management confirmed IPO proceeds will be fully deployed as per plan; analyst cited ~INR200 crore capex in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Magel Tyala tender pricing fell sharply as more bidders entered; management cited 8-9% price impact on realisation.
Raw material costs rose due to geopolitical factors, estimated at 3-3.5% margin impact; operating leverage ~1-1.5%.
Competition increased as PM KUSUM installations grew (about 1.5 lakh in FY24, 3.5 lakh in FY25, 5 lakh in FY26, per management).
Magel Tyala T6 tender bid submitted; financial bid opening expected in 7-10 days.
Solar EPC work in Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan has started execution.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin fall of ~24-25% to 15% is from pricing versus raw materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 8-9% to Magel Tyala bidding prices, 3-3.5% to raw material costs, and 1-1.5% to operating leverage, with value engineering limiting the impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15-17% EBITDA margin guidance inclusive of PM KUSUM 2.0?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The guidance is based on current bids, the Surya Ghar bids and channel sales; KUSUM 2.0 would lift margins slightly. Management said it assumed a slightly safer side.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR800-1,000 crore Surya Ghar revenue consistent with 20-25% growth on ~INR2,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the Surya Ghar figure is for FY27 Q2-Q4, not full-year. Q1 revenue of ~INR470 crore was mainly pumping. Conservatively, INR800 crore of business is assumed including the Magel Tyala T6 tender and wires and cables.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Surya Ghar margins versus KUSUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Surya Ghar margins are lower than KUSUM but the cumulative margin across businesses should be 15-17%. An analyst's reading of 12-15% for Surya Ghar was accepted as broadly correct.

qa_highlights.question: When will receivables normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 receivables to be better than Q1, with a larger improvement in Q3, but said the cash conversion cycle will not change much in Q2 because billing is running in parallel.

risks_watch: PM KUSUM 2.0 timing: repeated delays, and management said it cannot guarantee an August launch.
Receivable days at 229 with INR305 crore not yet due; cash conversion cycle at 244 days.
Margin sustainability: 15-17% guidance with Q1 at 15.7% operating margin, and the Surya Ghar margin likely below KUSUM.
Raw material and copper price volatility; management said any rise would affect the whole industry.
Execution of PM Surya Ghar 2 lakh installation target and inverter in-house timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on guidance and the recovery outlook, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly said PM KUSUM 2.0 timing is outside its control. Its answers on margin bridging and Surya Ghar economics were detailed but contained some internal inconsistencies, which reduces confidence.
